findings.note: The "nil-free JSON" assertion in TestFoldHappyPath can never fail. The guard is `strings.Contains(js, "null") && !strings.Contains(js, "\"prev_unfixed\":null")`, but on the happy path PrevUnfixed is always nil and Snapshot.PrevUnfixed carries `json:"prev_unfixed"` with no omitempty, so `"prev_unfixed":null` is always present and the second conjunct is always false. Verified by executing a probe over the same fold: the marshalled snapshot contains exactly one "null", and it is prev_unfixed. Any future nullable field that regresses to null would go undetected. A `strings.Count(js, "null") != 1` check (or a replace-then-Contains) would express the intended invariant.

evidence.note: Vacuous conjunction: the negated prev_unfixed clause is always false on this fixture.
PrevUnfixed *int `json:"prev_unfixed"` — no omitempty, so the key is always emitted as null when nil.

findings.note: The rewritten quickstart sentence misdescribes epic-ready twice. (a) It says task-done and PR-ready "add a Context Shard Plan", implying epic-ready has none, but epic-ready renders its own "## Context Shard Plan" section reading "Sharding is not applied to epic-ready reviews; see the child task-done and pr-ready packs." (b) It says "epic-ready renders 'not sharded'", but that literal string is the Review Manifest's Source-manifest-hash placeholder for any unsharded review, and epic-ready never renders a Review Manifest at all — its pack builder does not call reviewmanifest.Markdown. A reader grepping an epic-ready pack for "not sharded" will not find it.

evidence.note: epic-ready emits its own Context Shard Plan section and no Review Manifest section.
